sections.h2: Can I sell my Cedar Hill, TX house quickly for cash?
sections.html:
Yes. Cash is one of three Cedar Hill options, next to a full agent listing and a sale you run yourself. A cash buyer can often close faster because no lender is involved, though the price reflects repairs and risk. Ask for the offer in writing, and find out who pays for title work and what happens if the inspection turns up problems.

The house itself shapes the answer. A well-kept home on a quiet street may do better listed, while one with deferred repairs, tenants or tax trouble may suit a direct sale. Compare the net you would receive in each case.

sections.h2: What makes Cedar Hill different from other Dallas suburbs?
sections.html:
Cedar Hill sits about 18 miles southwest of downtown Dallas along US Highway 67, mostly in Dallas County with small parts in Ellis County, according to the city's parks master plan. It covers 35.2 square miles and has Joe Pool Lake on its western border and Cedar Hill State Park beside it.

  • The city calls itself the Hill Country of the Metroplex and holds the highest elevation in Dallas County, at 830 feet.
  • The Balcones Escarpment runs through the area, with rugged terrain between Joe Pool Lake and US 67.
  • Red Oak Creek and Bentle Branch Creek are the best-known creeks, and creeks flow away from the center of town.
  • The state park is 1,826 acres and, per the plan, is the most visited state park in Texas.

Hilly lots and nearby creeks mean drainage, foundation movement and flood questions come up often, so have surveys and repair records ready.

sections.h2: How did Cedar Hill start, and how fast did it grow?
sections.html:
The city says the settlement began in 1846 on land donated by an early settler who held a Peters Colony grant. The parks plan adds that Cedar Hill was once the county seat of Dallas County, that a tornado in 1856 destroyed most buildings, and that it incorporated in 1938.

Growth came late. The same plan shows 2,160 people in 1970, 6,847 in 1980 and 20,267 in 1990, a jump it ties to the completion of Joe Pool Dam in 1985 and the lake behind it. That means many houses date from the 1980s and later. Roofs, HVAC systems and original windows from that period may be near the end of their life, which buyers will price in.

sections.h2: Do Cedar Hill landlords have to register rentals?
sections.html:
Yes. The City Council adopted a Single Family Rental Registration Ordinance on November 10, 2020, with enforcement starting January 1, 2021. It covers single family rentals, including duplexes and townhomes, and owners register annually or when ownership changes. A tenant-occupied sale should include proof the registration is current.

Cedar Hill single family rental fees as the city lists them
ItemFee
Initial annual registration or change in ownership$50.00
Renewal$25.00
Late renewal$75.00
Residential Rental Certificate of Occupancy$25.00

Source: City of Cedar Hill, Single Family Rental Registration. A new certificate of occupancy is needed at each tenant change, and a code officer inspects the exterior within 30 days. Code Enforcement is at the Government Center, 285 Uptown Boulevard, and takes email at code@cedarhilltx.com.

sections.h2: How do homestead exemptions and tax limits work for Cedar Hill owners?
sections.html:
By state rule, school districts exempt $140,000 of a residence homestead, and an owner who is 65 or over, or disabled, receives $60,000 beyond that. Cities and counties may add their own, with a local option of up to 20 percent of value. Whether Cedar Hill's taxing units use that option is a question for the tax office of the county that bills your parcel.

  • School tax on a qualifying senior or disabled homestead is frozen at the first qualifying year's level.
  • That ceiling can move proportionately to a new Texas homestead if you buy again.
  • Disabled veterans receive an exemption scaled by rating, and a 100 percent rated veteran gets a full exemption on the homestead.
  • A buyer who takes a house after January 1 can claim the exemption for the rest of the year if the seller did not have it.

If a freeze applies to your house, tell your agent, since the buyer will not inherit it.

sections.h2: What if the Cedar Hill house is in a contract for deed, or goes to heirs?
sections.html:
A contract for deed, sometimes called a lease to own, falls under Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D when the buyer lives in the home, and the seller keeps title until payment is complete. The buyer has a statutory right to cancel, with notice periods in the code. If you hold one, ask a lawyer how it affects a sale.

For heirs, a transfer on death deed can pass real property without probate if it was recorded before the owner died. A Lady Bird deed lets the owner sell without the named beneficiary's consent. Without either, heirs may need a muniment of title or small estate affidavit before the deed can move.

sections.h2: How do I remove an occupant from a Cedar Hill house before selling?
sections.html:
Start with the right notice. A written notice to vacate usually gives at least three days unless the lease sets another period, and it can be handed to the tenant or a household member aged 16 or older, left inside the home in an obvious place, or mailed. Email counts only if the written lease allows it.

  • The suit is filed in justice court, and the tenant must be served at least four days before trial.
  • The hearing is set between 10 and 21 days after filing.
  • An appeal to county court must be filed within five days of judgment.
  • A writ of possession is available six days after final judgment, with 24 hours' notice before removal.

A person who stayed on after being told to leave, with no lease and no family tie, may be removable by a sheriff or constable request under Property Code chapter 24B instead of a court case. Wrongful removal can lead to a lawsuit, so confirm the facts with the sheriff's or constable's office first.

faqs.q: Is Cedar Hill in Dallas County or Ellis County?
faqs.a: Mostly Dallas County, with small portions in Ellis County. Your tax bill shows which county applies, and that decides the clerk and appraisal district for your parcel.

faqs.q: How much does Cedar Hill charge to register a rental?
faqs.a: The city lists $50 for the first annual registration or a change of owner, $25 to renew and $75 for a late renewal. A Residential Rental Certificate of Occupancy costs $25 at each tenant change. Confirm current fees with Code Enforcement.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cedar Hill house with a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes it subject to the lease unless it ends first. Make sure the rental registration is current, and expect a certificate of occupancy to be needed when the next tenant moves in.

faqs.q: What is the school homestead exemption near Cedar Hill?
faqs.a: Texas requires school districts to give $140,000, with $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. The exemption belongs to the owner who lives there. Buyers must apply themselves.

faqs.q: Can a Lady Bird deed help me sell?
faqs.a: It can. The owner keeps the right to sell or mortgage without the beneficiary's consent, and the property passes outside probate at death. Texas has no official form, so use a lawyer or the county clerk's guidance.
